CAGR is a smoothed average — it does not show year-to-year volatility.

📖 How to use

  1. Choose a mode: compute CAGR, or project from a CAGR.
  2. For CAGR: enter start value, end value and the number of years.
  3. For projection: enter start value, CAGR % and years.
  4. Read the CAGR, total return, doubling time — or the projected future value.

❓ Frequently asked questions

How is CAGR calculated?

CAGR = (end value / start value)^(1/years) - 1. It is the constant yearly rate that would grow the start value into the end value over the period.

What does CAGR actually tell me?

It smooths real, bumpy returns into a single average rate. Two investments can have the same CAGR with very different year-to-year volatility.

Can I project a future value from a CAGR?

Yes — switch to 'Project from CAGR' mode to grow a starting value at any CAGR you enter, for example your historical average.
